# Ornith token tally

**Generated by `./scripts/ornith-tally.sh --write`. Do not hand-edit — rerun it.**

What the local model has actually processed, per issue. Ornith runs in LM Studio on this
machine, so the real cost is $0.00; the hosted column is what the same traffic would have
cost on Sonnet 5 at list price ($3/MTok in, $15/MTok out), which is the model
`CLAUDE.md` says it replaces.

## Where these numbers come from

OpenCode's SQLite database, `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, which records
`tokens_input` and `tokens_output` on every session row.

This matters because **nothing else records it**. The dispatch logs in
`.switchyard-runs/` carry no token counts, LM Studio exposes no historical usage
endpoint, and a dispatcher subagent's `subagent_tokens` figure appears once in a
notification and is gone when the session ends. The database survives, which is why this
file is regenerable rather than a snapshot someone has to remember to update.

Issues are attributed by the session's working directory: a dispatch runs in
`../switchyard-NNNN`, so the worktree name is the issue number. That is another reason
a dispatch must never run in the primary checkout — it would land in `(main)` with no
issue attached.

Actual cost: **$0.00**. Ornith runs locally in LM Studio; the hosted column is what the
same traffic would have cost on Sonnet 5 at list price ($3/MTok in, $15/MTok out), which is
the model CLAUDE.md says it replaces.

## What the numbers say

**Input outweighs output by roughly 100 to 1.** That is the shape of an agentic loop
rather than anything about this model: every turn resends the accumulated context, so a
long round re-reads its own transcript hundreds of times. It is the strongest argument for
running the implementer locally — on a hosted model that ratio *is* the bill.

**The most expensive rounds are the ones that failed.** #0093 was killed at the timeout
having produced nothing usable. #0010 was split for being oversized. #0087 spent three
sessions, two of them on a test that asserted nothing. Well over half the total volume
went on rounds that were rejected or abandoned.

That is the cost of authoring defects, and it is invisible in the dollar column precisely
because it is free. Free failure is the kind that stops being noticed, which is why
`docs/review-failures.md` exists and why the preflight refuses a defective issue before
a round is spent on it.

**`(main)` covers sessions that predate the worktree rule**, run in the primary
checkout — exactly what `CLAUDE.md` now forbids.
